name: French Onion Pot Roast
desc: Chuck roast braised low with a big pot of caramelized onions, white wine and herbs, then shredded and baked under Gruyere.

source.title: French Onion Pot Roast
source.evidence: Identical ingredient list and amounts (3-4 lb chuck, 4 tbsp butter, 4 large onions, 3/4 cup Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio, 3 cups broth, 1 cup Gruyere) and the same 300°F, 3 1/2 hour braise.

ingredients.raw: 3-4 lb boneless chuck roast, excess fat trimmed
2 tsp kosher salt (about 1 tsp per side), plus more to taste
1 tsp ground black pepper (about 1/2 tsp per side)
3/4 cup dry white wine (Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio)
3 cups beef broth, plus more as needed
2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, plus more to taste

steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Pat the roast dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the roast without moving it until a golden brown crust forms, about 5 minutes per side. Set aside on a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and melt the butter in the same pot. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until light golden brown, 25-30 minutes. Add a splash of broth if brown bits stick.
Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes. Pour in the wine to deglaze and simmer until reduced by about half. Sprinkle in the flour and stir to coat.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme (tied with twine if you like). Bring to a simmer and season with salt and pepper.

Return the roast to the pot; the liquid should come at least three quarters of the way up the meat, so add more broth if needed. Cover tightly and braise in the oven for 3 1/2 hours, until fall-apart tender.
Take the pot out and raise the oven to 400°F. Shred the beef into chunks in the pot and discard excess fat, the bay leaves, and the herb stems.
Scatter the Gruyere over the top and return the pot to the oven until the cheese melts, 5-7 minutes.
Serve over mashed potatoes or with toasted baguette slices.
tips: For even more tender meat, braise an extra 20 minutes before shredding.
